I’d start with four Reels a week: one that makes people hungry, one that shows the craft, one that helps them choose, and one that gives them a reason to visit.

| Reel type | Opening hook | 4-shot list | Best day to try |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fresh out of the oven | “Sound on for this first crack.” | 1. Tray comes out of the oven. 2. Close-up of the golden crust. 3. Break one open and let the crunch play. 4. Set it on the counter with its name on screen. | Monday, to make a morning bakery stop tempting. |
| Behind the bake | “Here’s what happens before we open.” | 1. Flour hits the workbench. 2. Hands shape the dough. 3. Match-cut the raw tray to the baked batch. 4. Baker slides the first tray into the display. | Wednesday, for a midweek peek behind the counter. |
| This or that | “You get one box. Which side are you filling?” | 1. Open an empty pastry box. 2. Show the chocolate option with a close-up of the filling. 3. Show the fruit option with the same framing. 4. Put them side by side with “Chocolate or fruit?” on screen. | Thursday, when people can still plan a weekend pickup. |
| Weekend special | “This one’s only on the counter this weekend.” | 1. Lead with the finished special. 2. Show the final drizzle, dusting, or garnish. 3. Cut into it for the reveal. 4. Show it boxed with the price, pickup hours, and how to order. | Friday, before people settle their weekend plans. |

Treat those days as a starting test, not a rule. After four weeks, check Instagram Insights for which Reels earned shares and saves, and note which ones actually brought in orders.
